cells.document: Alexander Campbell, The Christian System, 2nd ed.
cells.section: Chapter VIII, The Purposes of God Concerning Man, paragraph X
cells.excerpt: all enjoyments shall be, as respects human agency, conditional; and that every man, in reference to spiritual and eternal blessings, shall certainly and infallibly have his own choice.
cells.shows: Campbell teaches that God's purposes are fixed in Christ while each person's share in spiritual blessings is conditional on that person's own choice.

cells.document: Alexander Campbell, The Christian System, 2nd ed.
cells.section: Chapter XVI, Baptism, paragraph VI (paragraph IV names penitent believers, not infants, as the proper subjects)
cells.excerpt: Baptism is, then, designed to introduce the subjects of it into the participation of the blessings of the death and resurrection of Christ
cells.shows: Baptism, given to penitent believers only, is taught as the act that brings a person into the blessings of Christ's death (the same chapter cites Acts 2:38, for the remission of sins), which pulls the tradition toward the sacramental side on baptism.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (one of two documents; this is the baptism half of a near-middle coordinate)

cells.document: Alexander Campbell, The Christian System, 2nd ed.
cells.excerpt: The breaking of the loaf and the drinking of the cup are commemorative of the Lord's death.
cells.shows: The Lord's Supper is described as a commemoration of Christ's death, which places the tradition on the memorial side for the Supper (Proposition VII of the same essay makes it part of every stated meeting).
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (the Supper half; memorial Supper plus baptism for remission of sins together give the audited 58)

cells.document: Alexander Campbell, Essays on the Work of the Holy Spirit in the Salvation of Men, No. III: Spiritual Gifts, in The Christian Baptist, vol. II no. 3
cells.excerpt: it is evident that these apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers, were all supernatural characters, for a precise object, and for a limited time
cells.shows: Campbell argues that the supernaturally gifted offices and the signs that went with them confirmed the apostolic testimony and were given only for a limited time.

cells.document: Alexander Campbell, The Christian System, 2nd ed.
cells.section: Kingdom of Heaven, under The Coming of the Kingdom / Present Administration of the Kingdom
cells.excerpt: Thus commenced the Reign of Heaven, on the day of Pentecost, in the person of the Messiah, the Son of God, and the anointed Monarch of the universe.
cells.shows: Campbell dates Christ's kingdom from Pentecost as a present reign and, in the same essay, gives its citizens the titles Israel of God and seed of Abraham, while holding that the laws of the kingdom are not to be sought in the Jewish scriptures.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (a present kingdom whose citizens inherit Israel's titles, with a sharp line between the Jewish and Christian institutions, fits a coordinate on the one-people side but short of the pole)

cells.document: Thomas Campbell, Declaration and Address of the Christian Association of Washington (first edition)
cells.excerpt: nothing ought to be inculcated upon christians as articles of faith; nor required of them as terms of communion; but what is expressly taught ... in the word of God.
cells.shows: The movement's founding document allows nothing to be made an article of faith or a term of communion except what Scripture expressly teaches.

cells.document: Alexander Campbell, The Christian System, 2nd ed.
cells.excerpt: These are all discretionary matters, and left to the prudence and good sense of the Christian communities--in other words, to the law of expediency.
cells.shows: Campbell holds that the New Testament gives no rule for the manner and arrangement of the assembly's acts, such as how the Supper is served, and leaves these to each congregation's judgment.

notes: This tradition rejects binding creeds on principle, so no cell is binding: every document here is a founding-generation text of the Stone-Campbell movement that both the a cappella Churches of Christ and the independent Christian Churches claim, labelled representative only. All seven excerpts were first read through WebFetch and then re-checked as exact substrings of the raw page text with curl (Abilene Christian University's mirror of the Memorial University Restoration Movement texts). Table is given two documents because the near-middle coordinate (58) is the sum of two different positions, not a split between parties: baptism of believers for the remission of sins, and a commemorative Supper. Worship is marked weaker: the Expediency chapter shows that the manner of worship is left to congregations, but the same movement holds that the acts of worship are fixed by the New Testament (Declaration and Address, Proposition 4, opened at the URL in the authority cell: 'the New Testament is as perfect a constitution for the worship, discipline and government of the New Testament church') and keeps the Supper in every Lord's Day meeting (Breaking the Loaf, Proposition VII), so 'free' here means no written liturgy or calendar, not an open-ended service. Kingdom: Campbell himself expected a future millennium brought in by the gospel (he named his journal The Millennial Harbinger); nothing opened in this pass addressed national Israel's future, so the excerpt supports the present-kingdom half of the coordinate only. Not opened and therefore not cited: any twentieth-century statement on instrumental music (the point that divides Churches of Christ from Christian Churches; it is not one of the six axes), and any modern representative statement from a Christian Churches body or college; a later pass could add one per axis for readers who want a living voice rather than Campbell. A footnote in The Christian Baptist vol. I no. 8 (1 March 1824) also reads 'since those gifts have ceased, the Holy Spirit now operates upon the minds of sinners only by the word', but it was seen only through the WebFetch summary and its authorship was not confirmed, so it is not used as a cell.
